source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Septoriose / Septoria leaf spot (caused by Septoria species) produces small, roundish spots on leaves, generally more numerous on the upper leaf surface, that can merge into larger blighted patches under humid conditions and cause premature leaf drop when infection is severe.

Like other fungal leaf diseases in this source, Septoria spreads through spores carried by rain-splash and wind during humid weather, and tends to be worse where trees are crowded and air circulation is poor, since leaves stay wet longer in such conditions.

Management follows the same general pattern as for other fungal leaf diseases described here: removing and destroying heavily infected leaf litter, improving airflow through appropriate spacing and pruning, and applying fungicide sprays during periods of high humidity when new infections are most likely to establish.
